# Animation Setup — Native Unity Animator wiring for the character roster

**Date:** 2026-05-19
**Slice:** Wire the KayKit-rigged characters (enemies / hero / pets / NPCs / bosses) to native Unity `Animator` controllers. No third-party animation engine.
**Status:** Source files written. The controller `.controller` assets are generated by an editor script the integrator runs in Unity; controller-to-prefab assignment is an open integrator step (no Unity access here — cannot build, run the script, or edit prefabs in the inspector).
**Design source:** `docs/enemy-codex.md` §5 ("Animation strategy & gap list").

## Files produced / edited

| File | Change | Purpose |
| ---- | ------ | ------- |
| `Assets/Editor/AnimatorSetup.cs` | **new** | Editor script — builds the `AnimatorController` assets via the `UnityEditor.Animations.AnimatorController` API. |
| `Assets/_Modules/Village/Enemies/Enemy.cs` | **edited** | Drives the enemy Animator — `Speed` from the NavMeshAgent velocity, `Attack`/`Hit` triggers, `Dead` bool. |
| `Assets/_Modules/Dungeons/DungeonHero.cs` | **edited** | Drives the hero Animator — `Speed` from the planar move speed. |
| `Assets/_Modules/Pets/Pet.cs` | **edited** | Drives the pet Animator — `Speed` from per-frame displacement, `Attack`/`Hit`/`Dead`. |
| `Assets/_Modules/Village/Hero/HeroAbilities.cs` | **edited** | Fires the hero `Cast` trigger when a Q/W/E/R ability resolves. |

No `.asmdef` files were changed. `Animator` is part of `UnityEngine` core, so the gameplay modules need no new references. `DeNelle.Editor` does **not** reference the gameplay asmdefs — `AnimatorSetup.cs` touches no gameplay type at all (it only builds `.controller` assets), so the reflection-only constraint is satisfied trivially.

## The shared-rig strategy (codex §5.1)

The codex's key fact: **every KayKit humanoid shares one skeleton.** `Rig_Medium` covers the Skeletons pack, the Adventurers, and all the Mystery Monthly humanoids; `Rig_Large` covers the bulky bodies (Skeleton Golem, Frost Golem). So the whole 19-entity roster animates from a tiny set of controllers built once. `AnimatorSetup.cs` builds **six** controllers into `Assets/Generated/Animators/`:

| Controller | Rig | For | States | Parameters |
| ---------- | --- | --- | ------ | ---------- |
| `HumanoidEnemy.controller` | Rig_Medium | Walker, Warrior, Rogue, Caster, Reaper; Caveman, Tiefling | Idle, Move, Attack, Hit, Death | Speed, Attack, Hit, Dead |
| `LargeEnemy.controller` | Rig_Large | Hollow Brute / Bone-Golem, Frost Golem | Idle, Move, Attack, Hit, Death | Speed, Attack, Hit, Dead |
| `Boss.controller` | Rig_Medium | Necromancer, Apprentice, Vault Keeper, Inn-Keeper, Watcher, Wolfwarden Ph.1 | Idle, Move, Attack, Hit, Death, **Cast** | Speed, Attack, Hit, Dead, **Cast** |
| `Hero.controller` | Rig_Medium | The Keeper (village + dungeon hero) | Idle, Move, Attack, Hit, Death, **Cast** | Speed, Attack, Hit, Dead, **Cast** |
| `Pet.controller` | Rig_Medium | Aether Sprite, Flame Pup (humanoid-rig pets) | Idle, Move, Attack, Hit, Death | Speed, Attack, Hit, Dead |
| `Npc.controller` | Rig_Medium | Village townsfolk | Idle, Move | Speed |

`LargeEnemy.controller` falls back to the `Rig_Medium` clip library if no `Rig_Large` clips are found, so it is always a valid asset.

### Clips wired to each state

The KayKit Character Animations 1.1 FBXs (`Rig_Medium_*.fbx` / `Rig_Large_*.fbx`) import with `clipAnimations: []` — Unity has **not** split them into manually-named sub-clips. `AnimatorSetup.cs` therefore does **not** hard-code clip names: it scans every category FBX with `AssetDatabase.LoadAllAssetRepresentationsAtPath`, collects every `AnimationClip` sub-asset into one library per rig, and matches each state to a clip by case-insensitive keyword search:

- **Idle** ← `idle` / `rest` / `breathing`
- **Move** ← `walk` / `run` / `move` / `jog`
- **Attack** ← `1h_melee_attack` / `melee_attack` / `attack` / `slash` / `swing` / `shoot`
- **Hit** ← `hit` / `hitrecieve` / `recieve_hit` / `flinch` / `damage` / `impact`
- **Death** ← `death` / `die` / `dead`
- **Cast** (Boss/Hero) ← `cast` / `channel` / `spellcast` / `special` / `interact`

If a state finds no matching clip the state is **still created** with an empty `Motion` (the controller stays valid) and the miss is logged. This makes the script correct whether KayKit ships one-clip-per-FBX or many — and if the take-names differ from the keyword list, the integrator just drops the right clip onto the named state.

### Transitions

- **Idle ↔ Move** — gated on the `Speed` float (threshold `0.1`), no exit time, short blend — the locomotion blend.
- **Attack / Hit / Cast** — fired by their trigger from Idle/Move (and Attack also interruptible by Hit), no exit time; return to Idle on clip completion (`exitTime 0.85`).
- **Death** — gated on the `Dead` bool from *any* state, never transitions out (the character is destroyed/pooled afterward).

## The `-executeMethod` entry point

```
-executeMethod DeNelle.Editor.AnimatorSetup.BuildAnimators
```

Also available as the menu item **Defenders ▸ Animation ▸ Build Animator Controllers**. The method is idempotent — re-running it overwrites the `.controller` assets in place. It logs a summary: controllers built, any states left clip-less, and the integrator reminder.

## How the gameplay scripts drive the Animator

Each edited script resolves its Animator with `GetComponentInChildren<Animator>()` (the Animator lives on the KayKit mesh child of the rig, not the gameplay GameObject) and **null-guards every call** — a character with no Animator/controller still runs its full gameplay logic.

- **`Enemy.cs`** — `Awake` finds the Animator; `Update` pushes `Speed` from `NavMeshAgent.velocity.magnitude`; the contact-attack tick fires `Attack` in sync with each damage tick; `TakeDamage` fires `Hit` on a surviving hit; `Die` sets the `Dead` bool. `Die` now delays `Destroy` by `DeathHoldSeconds` (1.6s) **only when an Animator is present**, so the collapse clip is visible — `Died` is still raised immediately, so wave logic is unaffected. With no Animator the enemy is destroyed at once (the prior behaviour).
- **`DungeonHero.cs`** — `Awake` finds the Animator; `Update` pushes `Speed` from `_planarVelocity.magnitude`.
- **`Pet.cs`** — new `Awake` finds the Animator; `Update` pushes `Speed` from per-frame displacement (Pet moves kinematically — no agent/rigidbody velocity to read); `Attack` fires the `Attack` trigger; `TakeDamage` fires `Hit` or latches `Dead`.
- **`HeroAbilities.cs`** — `Awake` finds the Animator; `TryCast` fires the `Cast` trigger when a cast succeeds.

Parameter names are duplicated as string constants in `AnimatorSetup.cs` and as `Animator.StringToHash` hashes in the gameplay scripts — they **must stay in sync** (`Speed` / `Attack` / `Hit` / `Dead` / `Cast`).

## Integrator steps (open — needs Unity)

1. **Run the build** — `Defenders ▸ Animation ▸ Build Animator Controllers` (or the `-executeMethod` above). Confirm six `.controller` assets land in `Assets/Generated/Animators/` and check the console summary for any clip-less states.
2. **Assign controllers to the character prefabs / rigs.** The generated controllers are **not** auto-assigned — the editor script only builds the `.controller` assets. The integrator must set each rig's `Animator.runtimeAnimatorController`:
   - Enemy prefab (`Assets/Prefabs/Village/Generated/Enemy_HollowWalker.prefab`, built by `VillageSceneBuilder`) → `HumanoidEnemy.controller`. The skeleton mesh child needs an `Animator` component — the KayKit FBX adds one on import for a rigged model; if the prefab's visual child has none, add one.
   - Hero rig (village hero near the Heart, built by `VillageSceneBuilder.BuildHero`; dungeon Keeper, built by `DungeonSceneBuilder.BuildHeroRig`) → `Hero.controller`. **NOTE:** both hero rigs currently use a placeholder capsule visual — once the real KayKit hero mesh is dropped in, put `Hero.controller` on its `Animator`.
   - Pet prefabs (deployed by `PetDeployer`) → `Pet.controller` — **except the Ice Wolf** (see GAP-PRIMARY below).
   - Boss bodies (Necromancer wave-boss, dungeon mini-bosses) → `Boss.controller`.
   - Heavy bodies (Hollow Brute, Frost Golem) → `LargeEnemy.controller`.
   - NPC townsfolk → `Npc.controller`.

   This could be folded into the scene builders later (e.g. `VillageSceneBuilder.EnsureEnemyPrefab` could `LoadAssetAtPath` the controller and set it via `SerializedObject` on the `Animator`), but as of this slice it is flagged as a manual integrator step to keep the change surgical.
3. **Verify the KayKit FBX import keeps the rig.** `AssetImportPostprocessor` forces `animationType = Generic` for rigged KayKit models — correct for `Animator` use. The character mesh FBXs must import with an Avatar; the Character Animations clips retarget onto the shared skeleton automatically because the rigs are identical.
4. **Clip-name reconciliation** — if the build summary reports clip-less states, open the FBX in `Assets/Models/KayKit/KayKit Character Animations 1.1/Animations/fbx/` and either (a) split + name the clips in the importer, then re-run the build, or (b) drag the right clip onto the named state in the controller.

## Known gaps (carried from codex §5.3)

- **GAP-PRIMARY — the quadruped wolf.** `Werewolf_Wolf` (Feral Wolf enemy, Wolfwarden Phase 2, **the Ice Wolf pet**) does **not** share the humanoid `Rig_Medium`/`Rig_Large` skeleton — none of these controllers retarget to it. `Pet.controller` is built for the humanoid pets only; the Ice Wolf needs its own controller built from the Werewolf Mystery Monthly pack's own bundled clips. This is **not** solved by `AnimatorSetup.cs` and is flagged here. When the wolf rig is audited, add a `BuildWolfController` to the editor script keyed off the Werewolf pack's clips.
- **GAP-1 — Cellar Hollow kneel-and-rock idle.** A bespoke clip; not in the shared library. The Cellar Hollow runs `HumanoidEnemy.controller` with a standard idle until the clip is commissioned.
- **GAP-2 — bespoke boss special gestures.** `Boss.controller`'s single `Cast` state rides on a substitute `Special`/`channel` clip — adequate per the codex (LOW priority). A per-boss bespoke clip would just replace the `Cast` state's `Motion`.
- **GAP-3 — man→wolf transform (Wolfwarden).** A model swap masked by VFX, not an animation clip — out of scope for the controller build.
- The Watcher's "fade" death is a dissolve **shader**, not an animation — `Boss.controller`'s `Death` state still plays a collapse; the dissolve is layered on top by VFX.
